scope: Critical source / novelty audit, no implementation or experiment.
root_review_corrections: decouple_rw=0 synchronizes virtual request generation, not physical address translation completion. decouple_rw=1 is not required for early physical AW.
Actual RAW_COUPLING_AVAIL=0, not backend defaults, determines absence of R-to-AW coupling.

First R is sufficient to show translation for that read burst, but does not universally cover all source bursts needed for an independently split write. Coupler can be a strong baseline for matching bursts.
Banked path uses original ID based banks and per-bank AW-first controller; do not reduce its entire behavior to only two differences.
Read/write channel and ttype distinguish direction. Missing explicit pair tag does not prove pairing impossible: descriptor or constrained ordering can suffice.
K denotes complete or partial pair-result holding records in a proposed baseline. Existing one/two request control slots are NOT K=1/2 pair records; revision tables that say so remain rejected.
Pair-result storage need not pin two TLB ways. Invalidated results must not be reused; keeping still-valid cache entries is optional, not mandatory.
NO_ERROR_HANDLING is not a replay capability.
CQ PR/PW TODO is an implementation limitation, not a field-wide innovation gap. No complete current-platform update-drain deadlock established.

Source-first credit plus all-source-reads-issued write admission is a root conditional argument under explicit physical-request drain/fair-service assumptions, not an experiment or a claimed novel algorithm.
Single-chunk timing algebra is illustrative. A pipelined multi-slot pretranslation baseline may hide the same delay; no measured advantage claimed.
Suspected cqh advance semantics was not audited end-to-end and is not promoted to a bug finding or paper contribution.
